summary: Indonesia postponed the execution of Mary Jane Veloso, a Filipina mother convicted of drug trafficking, while eight other death row prisoners were executed. The reprieve followed the surrender of her alleged recruiter in the Philippines, where authorities are investigating human trafficking allegations. Veloso's lawyers and supporters say she unknowingly carried heroin hidden in luggage supplied to her after a promised job fell through. Indonesian President Joko Widodo said the delay respects the Philippine legal proceedings but does not cancel her execution. Her family and supporters celebrated the decision after widespread appeals for clemency, including from Philippine President Benigno Aquino and boxer Manny Pacquiao.

Chris Rock posted photos documenting three police traffic stops in seven weeks, prompting debate about racial profiling and the experience known as driving while black. Federal statistics reported in 2013 showed Black people were about 30% more likely than white people to be pulled over. Rock did not explain the stops' outcomes. Many Twitter users supported him, while others accused him of race-baiting. Actor Isaiah Washington drew criticism for advising Rock to adapt, saying he replaced his Mercedes with Priuses to avoid repeated stops. Rock has previously used comedy to highlight racial disparities in policing.

Grace of Monaco, starring Nicole Kidman as Grace Kelly, will premiere on Lifetime on May 25 instead of receiving a U.S. theatrical release. The Weinstein Co. sold the film to the network after poor reviews and disappointing international performances. Once considered a possible Oscar contender, the film faced repeated release delays and a dispute between director Olivier Dahan and Harvey Weinstein over its final cut. Kelly's children also criticized it as historically inaccurate. The story follows Kelly during Monaco's early-1960s tax dispute with France as she considers returning to Hollywood.

John Travolta says he has not watched HBO's critical Scientology documentary Going Clear and has no interest in doing so. Citing 40 years of positive experiences with the church, he attributed the documentary to disgruntled former participants and said its allegations did not reflect his own experience. Travolta also credited Scientology with helping him cope with the death of his teenage son, Jett, in 2009. The documentary is based on Lawrence Wright's book about the organization and its Hollywood connections.

A natural gas line explosion at a law enforcement shooting range in Fresno, California, injured 11 people, including inmates assigned to maintenance work. The blast occurred where a county worker was operating a front loader, but its cause remains under investigation. One inmate was airlifted to a hospital, and both that inmate and the worker underwent emergency surgery; other injuries were mostly burns. Two deputies who helped rescue the injured also received treatment for ringing ears and sunburn-like symptoms. Firefighters extinguished the blaze, which left a crater and a blackened front loader.

Lady Antebellum singer Hillary Scott's tour bus caught fire on Interstate 30 near Dallas on Thursday after a rear tire blew out. Scott, her husband, the tour manager and the driver all exited safely before the bus burst into flames. Scott said the fire destroyed everything in the back lounge except her Bible and thanked those who helped keep them safe. Bandmates Charles Kelley and Dave Haywood were not aboard. The group was scheduled to perform Sunday at the Academy of Country Music Awards in Arlington, Texas.

Gwyneth Paltrow is taking part in the Food Bank for New York City's challenge to spend just $29 on food for one week, or about $1.38 per meal, to raise awareness of the difficulties faced by people receiving food stamps. Nominated by chef Mario Batali, she shared a photo of groceries including leafy greens, dried beans and rice. Organizers launched the challenge in response to food stamp cuts, which they say increased demand at soup kitchens and food pantries, and hope it will build understanding of families' struggles to afford food.

Malaysia, Australia and China announced plans to double the underwater search area for missing Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 if the initial 60,000-square-kilometer zone yields no wreckage. Searchers had covered about 60% of that area without finding the aircraft and expected to finish in May. Searching the additional zone could take another year and would cover all areas considered highly probable. Flight 370 disappeared on March 8, 2014, with 239 people aboard while traveling from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. Satellite data indicated it ended up in the southern Indian Ocean, but its exact location and the reason it veered off course remain unknown.

Christopher Scarver told the New York Post that Jeffrey Dahmer's disturbing jokes and apparent lack of remorse helped motivate him to kill the serial murderer in prison in 1994. Scarver alleged that Dahmer fashioned food into fake body parts with ketchup as blood. Dahmer's former prison minister separately described his cannibalism jokes as morbid humor used to cope with imprisonment. Scarver said he confronted Dahmer with an article about his crimes before striking him with a metal bar, then killed fellow inmate Jesse Anderson. Scarver received two life sentences for the killings.
